Time to Inactivity: Survival Analysis of Online Retail II Customers

Kaplan-Meier, log-rank tests and Cox proportional hazards (R validation layer)

Author

Customer Lifecycle, Churn & CLV project

Published

October 14, 2026

Question and event definition

Python’s churn model answers who is likely to lapse in the next 90 days. This report asks when customers lapse after acquisition and which acquisition-time characteristics shift that timing.

  • Event (lapse) - the first inter-purchase gap longer than 90 days (same 90-day horizon as the churn proxy). This is an inactivity proxy, not an observed cancellation.
  • Duration - active days from first purchase to the last purchase before the lapse (+1 day, so a customer who never returns has duration 1).
  • Censoring - customers with no observable lapse by the data end minus 90 days.
  • Covariates are fixed at acquisition (first-order value, first-order product count, country, acquisition quarter). End-of-period RFM scores are deliberately not used: they are computed from the outcome period and would create immortal-time bias.
  • Customers first seen in Dec-2009 are left-truncated (the extract starts then) and are excluded from the main analysis; a sensitivity check includes them.

Overall survival

4305 customers, 3997 lapse events (92.8%).

Code 
kable(rd("km_overall.csv"), digits = 3, caption = "Kaplan-Meier: share of customers without a 90-day lapse")
Kaplan-Meier: share of customers without a 90-day lapse
time survival lower upper n_risk
1 0.409 0.395 0.424 4305
2 0.407 0.393 0.422 1761
30 0.347 0.333 0.362 1455
90 0.192 0.180 0.204 758
180 0.102 0.093 0.112 360
365 0.041 0.035 0.049 107

The survival curve drops by roughly 60% at day 1: most customers’ first purchase is followed by a gap of more than 90 days. Activation after the first order is therefore the dominant lifecycle problem.

Proportional-hazards check (cox.zph)

Code 
kable(rd("cox_zph.csv"), digits = 4)
term chisq df p_value
log_first_value 1.2106 1 0.2712
log_first_products 1.2869 1 0.2566
country_group 1.1478 4 0.8866
acq_quarter 15.8490 3 0.0012
GLOBAL 18.0416 9 0.0347

Acquisition quarter violates PH (its effect varies over follow-up time, consistent with seasonal wholesale buying). The remedy is a Cox model stratified on acquisition quarter:

Sensitivity and limitations

Code 
cat(tail(readLines(file.path(out, "summary.txt")), 1))
Sensitivity incl. 2009-12 cohort: HR log_first_value = 0.826 (main: 0.882)
  • Lapse is a behavioural proxy; a customer may return after 90+ days (the event is “first lapse”, not permanent churn).
  • Covariates are acquisition-time only; the Python model covers time-varying behaviour.
  • Results are associations, not causal effects of order size.
